The *Gopālaka Sutta* (Ud 4.3; PTS Ud 38) is the third discourse in the fourth chapter (Meghiya Vagga) of the *Udāna*. The narrative describes a cowherd who, after making a food offering to the Buddha and the monastic community, is abruptly murdered. In response to this event, the Buddha utters an inspired verse of teaching (*udāna*) on the nature of the mind and harm. The provided secondary literature references do not discuss this discourse, referring instead to the homonymous *Mahāgopālaka Sutta* (MN 33) and *Cūḷagopālaka Sutta* (MN 34) of the Majjhima Nikāya.
